entry.title: Drift-Linked Wallet Sends $54.8 Million in ETH to Tornado Cash
entry.summary:
Wallets tied to the April 1 Drift Protocol exploit moved 25,700 ETH — about $61.56 million at current prices, the figure reported in the source body, while the headline cited $54.8 million — into the mixer Tornado Cash in batches over roughly two hours on Tuesday. The addresses had been inactive for about two months before the transfers.
The deposits are the second known mixing round by the exploiter, after about 23,095 ETH was sent to Tornado Cash on July 23 and 24, and they move a large part of the unrecovered haul further from recovery as Drift's DFX recovery pool pays early claimants roughly a penny per dollar of verified loss.
Arkham Intelligence data shows the deposits arrived in batches of 100 ETH — about $237,800 each — plus smaller 10 ETH chunks, sizes that match the mixer's fixed deposit pools. After the transfers, the 71 addresses tracked under the attacker entity still held 81,454 ETH, worth roughly $198.58 million, plus about $561,600 in USDT, USDC, Solana and USDY.

entry.title: A new centralized laundering service FreedomXMR (FXMR) appeared on Hyperliquid C
entry.summary:
On-chain investigator ZachXBT reported that FreedomXMR (FXMR), a centralized money-laundering service that appeared on Hyperliquid Core in August 2026, has more than 87% of its inflow volume tied directly to illicit activity. A manual review of all historical FXMR inflows above $10,000 traced over $20 million to ransomware, exploit, malware and social-engineering incidents, and the supporting spreadsheet was shared with the Hyperliquid team.
The disclosure names Hyperliquid Core as a channel repeatedly used by laundering services, and ZachXBT said the chain has previously hosted operations such as b1exch that exploit its permissionless design. The evidence has been handed to the Hyperliquid team, but no confirmation of action by the team was reported.
The traced incidents include the DCENT Wallet, Fetch.ai and Axelar exploits and an unnamed ransomware payment in September 2026, plus the Gamdom exploit in October 2026. ZachXBT said the FXMR admin sources XMR liquidity from KuCoin with more than 3,000 deposits to the exchange, likely using a swap model similar to Wagyu's; the FXMR ticker was bought in a Hyperliquid auction on July 27, 2026 for 518.28 HYPE (about $28,000).

entry.title: FN Brief | Launching After Two Delays, Aero Bids Farewell to the ve(3,3) Economic Model
entry.summary:
Aero completed its twice-delayed merger launch and replaced its ve(3,3) tokenomics with a revenue-linked model, scrapping weekly voting and the fixed emission schedule while expanding to seven chains. The team said the protocol has earned more than $500 million for holders on Base.
The overhaul changes how incentives and governance work at Base's main liquidity hub: weekly vote-directed emissions give way to a system tied to protocol revenue.
The ve(3,3) design it abandons combined Curve-style vote escrow with Olympus DAO's (3,3) mechanism, in which lockers vote on where emissions go each epoch. Aero's replacement ties token economics to revenue and drops both the weekly voting cycle and the fixed emission table.

entry.title: Mastercard opens early access to AI agent payments following pilots with Coinbase, Base and Cloudflare
entry.summary:
Mastercard has opened early access to a system called Agent Pay for Machines, which lets autonomous software agents discover services, agree to terms and pay for them within human-set spending limits. The company unveiled the milestone at Cloudflare's Connect conference, where Mastercard's Jorn Lambert demonstrated a live transaction.
Mastercard frames the system as a fix for a specific friction: paid online services typically require an account, API key or billing relationship with each provider, which breaks down when an agent selects services on the fly. The launch follows end-to-end pilots with Cloudflare, Ant International, AWS, BVNK and Coinbase.
Agent Pay for Machines builds on the open x402 protocol: when an agent hits a paid service returning a "402 Payment Required" response, it generates a digitally signed payment voucher that the provider verifies before delivering the service, with vouchers batchable for later redemption. In the demo, an agent for marketing agency Hype ran a protein-bar campaign across nine payments to two independent merchants on a single budget, with Coinbase supplying the wallet, Base providing on-chain settlement, and BVNK handling fiat or stablecoin settlement through Mastercard's Global Money Platform; Mastercard is also releasing buyer- and seller-side APIs, a developer toolkit and a testing environment.

entry.title: Webull to Open Perpetual Futures Trading to US Users in November, Initially Covering Bitcoin and Other Crypto Assets
entry.summary:
Online investment platform Webull (NASDAQ: BULL) will begin offering perpetual futures trading to eligible US customers starting in November, with Bitcoin and other crypto assets among the first products, and plans to widen access before the end of the year. The contracts will be listed on KalshiEX, a CFTC-designated contract market, and cleared by Kalshi Klear, a CFTC-regulated derivatives clearing organization, and can be traded directly through existing Webull futures accounts.
The launch gives futures-approved US retail clients access to crypto perpetual futures through CFTC-regulated venues, a product that has largely traded on offshore platforms for US users. Access is limited at first to customers already approved for futures trading.
Webull said the rollout starts in November with a planned expansion of eligibility by year-end; trading runs through existing Webull futures accounts rather than a new crypto-specific product line. The products are listed on KalshiEX and cleared by Kalshi Klear.

entry.title: Strive's Preferred Stock SATS Lists on Nasdaq, Raising $630 Million in IPO With a 15% Annual Fixed Dividend
entry.summary:
Strive, a Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin treasury company chaired by Matt Cole, closed an upsized IPO of its SATS preferred stock on Oct. 20, selling 7 million shares at $90 each for $630 million in gross proceeds and listing the stock on Nasdaq. The preferred carries a 15% annual fixed dividend on its $100 stated amount, is cumulative, and is scheduled to be paid each business day starting Nov. 9, subject to board declaration.
The deal gives public-market investors a daily-paid, 15%-yielding instrument issued by a Bitcoin treasury company, and Strive has said proceeds may fund additional Bitcoin purchases alongside working capital and income-generating assets. However, the company has not specified how much of the proceeds will actually go to Bitcoin.
Strive estimated net proceeds of about $608.15 million after underwriting discounts, commissions and expenses; at an illustrative Bitcoin price of $82,500, that amount could buy roughly 7,372 BTC, which would lift reported holdings from 36,818 BTC to about 44,190 BTC and potentially exceed Metaplanet's reported 44,000 BTC. At the $90 IPO price, the $15 annual stated dividend equals about 16.67% of the purchase price, and chief risk officer Jeff Walton said the company carries no debt or maturities and is focused on a single obligation: paying dividends.

entry.title: Liquid Says Bitcoin Swaps Are Restored While Peg-Outs Stay Frozen
entry.summary:
Liquid said it has restored Bitcoin swap trading on its network, but peg-outs remain frozen, leaving users unable to redeem L-BTC for BTC on the Bitcoin mainchain amid an ongoing security incident.
The continued peg-out freeze means service restoration is only partial: users can trade on Liquid, but the path for moving value back to Bitcoin’s mainchain remains closed.
Liquid’s peg-out mechanism converts L-BTC back to BTC on the Bitcoin mainchain; restoring swaps does not by itself reopen that redemption channel.

entry.title: Coinbase will convert USDT, DAI, PYUSD to USDC on Oct 30, triggering taxable events under German law.
entry.summary:
Coinbase will automatically convert German users' USDT, DAI and PYUSD balances into USDC on October 30. Because the exchange is converting the assets on users' behalf, the swap is treated as a taxable event under German law rather than a neutral balance change.
The policy forces affected German users to hold USDC and, per the source, leaves them with a tax liability attached to a conversion they did not initiate. It also shows an exchange steering stablecoin balances toward its own preferred dollar token in a single jurisdiction.
The conversion is scheduled for October 30 and applies to three third-party stablecoins — Tether's USDT, MakerDAO's DAI and PayPal's PYUSD — while leaving USDC untouched. The source frames the resulting tax treatment alongside Germany's one-year holding-period rule for private crypto holdings.

entry.title: JPMorgan predicts Bitcoin will be the highest-return asset of the next decade, beating US stocks and gold
entry.summary:
J.P. Morgan Asset Management's 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, released Monday, Oct. 19, included bitcoin for the first time, projecting a 10% compound annual return over the next 10 to 15 years. That tops its forecasts for US large-cap stocks (7.5%), US REITs (8.2%), gold (5.5%) and a classic 60/40 stock-bond portfolio (7%), with an arithmetic mean return of 20.9% and 55% annualized volatility.
Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan framed the inclusion as a sign of traditional financial institutions' shifting stance toward crypto. The forecast comes from the asset management arm of the largest US bank, putting bitcoin on the same table as mainstream assets in a report institutional allocators use as reference.
JPMorgan said that "for the first time, we put a range on bitcoin returns, though we do not yet include bitcoin in our main covariance matrices," and instead built a separate, smaller comparison matrix, citing volatility and unstable correlations. The report also pushed back on a popular bull case, calling the idea that currency debasement will spark a rush into crypto "wide of the mark."

entry.title: German savings banks begin phased rollout of cryptocurrency trading services
entry.summary:
Germany's savings banks (Sparkassen) began a phased rollout on Oct. 19 allowing customers of the first participating institutions to trade cryptocurrencies through their existing Sparkasse apps, according to the German Savings Banks and Giro Association (DSGV). The initial lineup covers BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL and POL, with each savings bank setting its own go-live date and 30 to 40 additional institutions expected to join each month.
The move opens regulated retail crypto trading inside Germany's dominant local banking network, which DSGV's own website counted at 337 independent savings banks as of August 2026, with the association targeting coverage of most interested institutions by the first half of 2027.
The service is provided by DekaBank, the group's securities services provider, with crypto assets custodied by DekaBank in cooperation with the Stuttgart Stock Exchange, at a fee of about €0.99 (US$1.11) per order. DSGV said the offering targets customers who want to buy, sell and custody crypto themselves; the savings banks will not provide investment advice or market the service broadly, and will explicitly warn of sharp price swings and the risk of total loss.

entry.title: THORChain Targets Rujira Restart With v3.21 Exploit Fix
entry.summary:
THORChain is preparing a v3.21 protocol upgrade that patches the exploit in Rujira's FIN contract and is intended to allow the halted App Layer to restart. The network is targeting block 28,366,100, expected around Friday, Oct. 23, according to its release notes.
Rujira is THORChain's App Layer, so the exploit forced its trading and liquidity functions to halt until the patch is deployed. A node-operator restart is still required after the upgrade, meaning the restart depends on operator participation rather than the code release alone.
The fix is specifically aimed at the FIN contract exploit on Rujira, and THORChain has set an upgrade block height with an expected activation date of around Oct. 23. The release notes state that a node-operator restart is still needed for the App Layer to come back online.

entry.title: JPMorgan Brings Deposit Token to Ethereum for Institutional Clients
entry.summary:
JPMorgan has launched its JPM Coin deposit token on Ethereum for institutional clients, and holders can now move the token between Ethereum and Coinbase's Base network. Each unit represents a dollar already held in a JPMorgan account and is redeemable for dollars at any time with no lock-up, but only vetted, approved counterparties are permitted to hold it.
The move puts a regulated bank-deposit liability on a public blockchain, extending tokenized-deposit settlement beyond a single proprietary or Layer 2 network. Emma Landriault, global head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan's blockchain unit, framed it as part of a year of "further convergence between Wall Street and crypto."
JPMorgan expects crypto firms to use the token for payments while financial institutions use it to settle trades in tokenized assets or post collateral. Kinexys has processed more than $4 trillion in transactions at roughly $7 billion a day, compared with about $12 trillion a day across JPMorgan's broader payments business.

entry.title: Coinbase Links US and Offshore Crypto Derivatives Markets via Deribit
entry.summary:
Coinbase is linking its US derivatives business with Deribit's offshore derivatives marketplace, a move reported by Startup Fortune as expanding cross-market access to crypto derivatives trading. Coinbase support pages describe the effort as combining Coinbase International Exchange's global reach with Deribit's derivatives technology into a unified trading platform, and CryptoTimes reported on Oct. 7, 2026 that the integration had been completed.
Coinbase says combining the two venues is intended to deliver deeper liquidity, faster execution and a stronger risk framework, and to support new product offerings. The link gives US-facing accounts a route into Deribit's offshore derivatives order books.
According to CryptoTimes, the completed integration unites US and global crypto derivatives liquidity and expands access to options, spot margin and unified portfolios. Coinbase's own help pages describe the two platforms as joining forces to create a single derivatives trading experience.

entry.title: Mesh partners with Visa to enable direct spending of crypto balances
entry.summary:
Crypto payments network Mesh announced a strategic partnership with Visa that lets users of participating digital wallets and platforms pay directly with cryptocurrency, stablecoin and fiat balances across Visa's global acceptance network, both in stores and online. Mesh provisions a Visa payment credential in the background so users can tap a standard contactless terminal, while merchants keep receiving funds through their normal Visa checkout flow.
The integration removes the need to pre-sell or transfer assets to a bank account, or to obtain a separate crypto card, before spending wallet balances at merchants. Visa said its network covers more than 175 million merchant locations across over 200 countries and territories.
Mesh will act as program manager, handling customer onboarding and KYC as well as funding and conversion between cryptocurrencies, stablecoins and fiat for each transaction. First launch timing, supported devices and participating platforms will be announced once rollout details are finalized.

entry.title: Metaplanet Approved to Take Control of Nasdaq-Listed SLE, Completing Its US Listing Footprint
entry.summary:
Metaplanet founder and CEO Simon Gerovich said on Oct. 19 that the company's deal with Nasdaq-listed Super League Enterprise (SLE) was formally approved at the company's shareholder meeting. Metaplanet will contribute 2,100 BTC plus $2.5 million in cash, worth roughly $134.6 million, in exchange for about 44.86 million newly issued common shares at $3 per share plus preferred stock and warrants, giving it control of SLE.
Gerovich said that after closing, the company will serve as Metaplanet's US-listed Bitcoin treasury platform, giving it direct access to US capital markets and more flexible financing. Combined with Metaplanet Securities in Japan, the approval gives the firm complementary platforms in the two largest capital markets.
Metaplanet will hold about 95.7% of SLE's issued common shares per BlockBeats, while a Cointelegraph report on the same approval put the ownership stake at 93.7%. Super League plans to rebrand as Superplanet with the Nasdaq ticker SUPA, intends to finance further Bitcoin purchases mainly through senior non-convertible perpetual preferred stock rather than debt, and Metaplanet holds an option to invest up to $210 million in junior preferred stock; Metaplanet's common shares are subject to a five-year lock-up.

entry.title: Introducing Binance AI Pro
entry.summary:
Binance announced the global rollout of Binance AI Pro, a finance-focused AI agent that converts trading ideas described in conversation into tested, automated strategies whose parameters are set by the user. The rollout covers the Binance website and app for all users globally starting 2026-10-19.
Binance says the product lets users build automated strategies without coding, lowering the technical barrier to strategy automation for retail users on one of the largest exchanges.
Strategies are first tested through simulated trading and deployed to live trading only after user approval; each live strategy runs in a separate sub-account, and funds can only be moved manually by the user. A free Standard tier offers a 250,000 monthly quota with access to the DeepSeek model, while a Premium tier at 19.99 USDC per month offers a 10 million monthly quota and access to models including ChatGPT Sol, ChatGPT Astra and Claude Opus, depending on region; the earlier Beta version continues to run and users can migrate chat history and strategies to the new version.

entry.title: 1.404 Wallets Drained on an Altcoin: Network Halted, Exchanges Take Action!
entry.summary:
Koin Bülteni reported that 1,404 wallets were drained on an unnamed altcoin network, after which the network was halted and exchanges took protective action. The report does not name the affected asset or quantify the losses in the excerpt.
The network halt and exchange countermeasures indicate the incident is being handled as a live compromise affecting holders on that chain, rather than an isolated individual wallet theft.
The headline figure is 1,404 wallets drained. The affected asset, the attack vector and any loss estimate are not disclosed in the source excerpt.

entry.title: BlackRock files for bitcoin ETF offering downside protection and upside exposure to IBIT
entry.summary:
BlackRock has filed for a bitcoin ETF that seeks to provide downside protection while keeping upside exposure to its existing iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT). The product is at the regulatory filing stage and has not been approved or launched.
If approved, the filing would give BlackRock a second bitcoin ETP wrapper aimed at investors who want bitcoin-linked returns with a measure of loss buffering, rather than direct spot exposure through IBIT.
The filing ties the new fund's upside exposure to IBIT, BlackRock's existing spot bitcoin ETF, which is designed to track the price of bitcoin through an exchange-traded product. Comparable protected-bitcoin products already on the market, such as Calamos' structured-protection ETFs and CBOJ, pair bitcoin-linked exposure with Treasuries and options overlays.

entry.title: The Crypto Devices Built to Foil Hackers Came With Spies Inside
entry.summary:
Bloomberg published an investigation on October 18, 2026 reporting that crypto hardware devices marketed as resistant to hacking shipped with embedded surveillance or spy components. The report describes the problem as originating inside the devices themselves rather than from an external attack.
Hardware wallets are sold on the premise that private keys stay isolated inside a dedicated device; embedded surveillance components undercut that premise for the affected products. The finding shifts scrutiny to device manufacturing and distribution rather than to software vulnerabilities alone.
The reporting frames the issue as a supply-chain and privacy problem rather than a protocol exploit, and no confirmed loss of user funds has been reported.

entry.title: Nine U.S. Issuers Block Their Shares From Trading on OKXICE Token Platform
entry.summary:
Nine U.S. issuers have moved to block their shares from trading on OKXICE's token platform, restricting tokenized equity trading on the venue. The action targets multiple tokenized equity instruments tied to U.S.-listed companies that the platform intended to offer.
The move signals legal and operational risk for tokenized securities venues, as issuer consent can determine whether tokenized shares of a given company remain tradable on a platform.
OKXICE is the OKX–ICE tokenized stock venture that filed with the SEC to offer tokenized shares in more than 60 U.S.-listed companies, with one report citing 63 NYSE-listed names, under the agency's Innovation Exemption.

entry.title: ⚡️Qubic Discloses Security Incident: Roughly 2.94 Trillion QU Stolen From 1,404 Qubic Wallets
entry.summary:
Qubic disclosed that between 23:42 UTC on Oct. 17 and 01:26 UTC on Oct. 18, an attacker exploited insufficient randomness in some wallets' Seed generation to access and transfer about 2.94 trillion QU from 1,404 Qubic wallets. The network was halted at tick 85,371,949, and the seed-generation flaw was fixed in version 4.26.4.
Qubic said the problem lies in the Seed generation mechanism rather than the Qubic protocol itself, and that 87.1% of the stolen funds remain on the Qubic network and have been frozen, while the remaining 12.9% sent to MEXC has also been frozen in the receiving accounts.
Qubic listed the affected seeds as those created in any browser on iPhone or iPad before Oct. 18, those created in Safari on Mac before the same date, and those created through the Qubic iOS app before July 2025. Follow-up handling will be decided by the Computor quorum under network rules, with a full technical report to be published once a fund-recovery plan is set; The Defiant reported the drain as worth about $1.3 million.

entry.title: Starknet research proposal on whether to continue transitioning into an L1 currently has 99.95% support
entry.summary:
On Snapshot, the research proposal asking whether Starknet should continue its transition into an independent L1 is currently passing with more than 345 million votes in favor (99.95%), against roughly 157,700 votes opposed (0.05%). Voting is scheduled to close on October 22.
The tally is a near-unanimous signal from participating voters on a structural architectural question — whether one of the largest ZK rollups keeps moving toward standalone L1 status — although it is a research proposal and does not itself execute any upgrade.
Snapshot is an off-chain, gas-free voting tool, and the outcome of this research proposal is a sentiment signal rather than an on-chain change. StarkWare has said the L1 move remains under evaluation rather than decided, describing it as the network's clearest strategic path forward.

entry.title: Cysic cross-chain bridge attacked, hacker minted 10 million CYS without authorization
entry.summary:
The Cysic Foundation said its cross-chain bridge was exploited on October 17, when an attacker gained unauthorized access to a database supporting the bridge service and used a processing logic flaw to submit a fake mint message, creating 10 million CYS on BNB Smart Chain. The unauthorized mint occurred at 12:31:38 UTC, and Cysic added the recipient address to the token contract's blacklist at 13:47:52 UTC.
About 2.8 million CYS remained at the blacklisted address and can no longer be transferred out. Cysic said the incident was confined to bridge message processing and minting, and did not affect the mainnet, other operational systems, or existing assets in user wallets.
Cysic said the 10 million tokens minted does not by itself establish the final dollar loss, and that transfers, swaps and actual losses remain under review; roughly 160.8 million CYS were in circulation at the time, according to CoinMarketCap data cited in reports. The foundation has hired an unnamed security firm to investigate the attack path and trace the funds, and said the bridge will reopen only after a security review is completed.

entry.title: Binance is shutting down its bitcoin mining pool after hashrate crashed 65%
entry.summary:
Binance is shutting down its Bitcoin mining pool after the pool's hashrate dropped roughly 65%, ending the exchange's mining-pool service for customers.
Miners who directed hashpower to Binance Pool lose that option and must route their machines to other pools, removing one well-known exchange-operated pool from the choices available to them.
The roughly 65% decline refers to the Binance pool's own hashrate, not Bitcoin's network-wide hashrate. The pool was marketed as an exchange-integrated service with instant reward access, VIP perks and cloud mining features.

entry.title: DTCC's tokenization service launches with 25 securities, backed by roughly $30 trillion in underlying assets
entry.summary:
According to materials published by DTCC, its tokenization service has opened with 25 tokenizable securities whose underlying DTC-custodied assets total roughly $30 trillion. The tokens correspond 1:1 to the original securities, carry the same CUSIP, and can be transferred peer-to-peer 24/7 between registered DTC wallets subject to compliance transfer restrictions, while DTC remains the official book of record.
Because the tokens keep the same CUSIP and the same rights and investor protections as book-entry securities, a slice of DTC-custodied assets — including Treasury coupon and maturity servicing — now runs on blockchain rails without DTC ceding its role as the official record keeper.
The first supported assets are Russell 1000 constituents (starting with some large-cap stocks), selected ETFs and U.S. Treasuries; Treasury interest and maturity servicing will occur on-chain, with payments made in fiat to participants' traditional accounts. Initial networks are Canton Network (CIP-56) and DTCC's private Besu network (ERC-20), with Stellar (SEP-41) and Circle's Arc (ERC-20) expected to connect in 2027.

entry.title: Visa and Mastercard adopt USDC payouts across 200 countries
entry.summary:
Visa and Mastercard are enabling USDC payouts across roughly 200 countries, extending stablecoin settlement through the two largest global card networks, according to CryptoSlate. The reported rollout would let payouts be routed in the dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle rather than solely through traditional correspondent banking rails.
Stablecoin settlement through Visa and Mastercard would move USDC from crypto-native venues into mainstream payment infrastructure used by merchants and financial institutions. Search context indicates card networks are already testing multiple stablecoins side by side for settlement, making this a live contest over which dollar tokens sit on those rails.
The report frames the move as a payout expansion spanning about 200 countries. Search excerpts note that Mastercard expanded its stablecoin settlement support in June 2026 to include USDC, PYUSD, RLUSD and SoFiUSD, and that SoFi became the first bank-issued stablecoin to go live on a major card network.

entry.title: BNY and Citadel Securities Use Tokenized Treasury in Overnight Repo
entry.summary:
BNY (Bank of New York Mellon) and market maker Citadel Securities executed an overnight repurchase agreement in which a tokenized Treasury was used, according to The Defiant. The transaction places a blockchain-represented government debt instrument inside a core short-term institutional funding trade rather than in a standalone tokenization pilot.
Overnight repo is the plumbing through which institutions borrow and lend cash against Treasuries, so using a tokenized Treasury there signals tokenized real-world assets edging from investment products into collateral and settlement functions.
The trade was structured as an overnight repo, a short-term secured loan in which securities are sold and repurchased the next day. It involved BNY, a major custodian bank, and Citadel Securities, one of the largest Treasury market intermediaries.

entry.title: CoreWeave, Broadcom, Verizon among nine companies objecting to tokenized trading of their shares on OKXICE
entry.summary:
Nine companies, including CoreWeave, Broadcom and Verizon, have objected to OKXICE facilitating tokenized trading of their shares, The Block reported on Oct 17, 2026. The objections raise legal and market-structure questions for tokenized equities.
According to the report, the objections raise legal and market-structure questions for tokenized equities, as listed issuers push back against third parties offering token versions of their shares.
OKXICE is the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) that filed with the SEC on Oct 5, 2026 to launch a tokenized securities platform. Its notice covered more than 60 companies currently listed on US stock exchanges.

entry.title: Strategy Slides 9.6% After MSCI Decision, Outpacing Bitcoin’s Drop
entry.summary:
Strategy's shares fell 9.6% following an MSCI decision, a drop larger than bitcoin's decline over the same period. The move outpaced the underlying asset that dominates the company's balance sheet.
The gap between the share move and bitcoin's decline points to the stock's sensitivity to index treatment, a factor separate from the price of the bitcoin it holds.
Strategy is the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, and its equity is widely treated as a crypto-equity proxy. The decline exceeded bitcoin's own move rather than simply mirroring it.

entry.title: Binance Pool shuts on November 10, with record access ending two weeks later
entry.summary:
Binance Pool, the exchange's Bitcoin mining pool service, will shut down on November 10, and miners' access to their records will end two weeks after that date, giving users a deadline to move their operations elsewhere.
Miners who direct hashrate to Binance Pool must migrate to another pool before the November 10 shutdown, and the later record-access cutoff means payout and earnings data must be exported within that window.
Two separate deadlines apply: the pool itself stops operating on November 10, while access to records continues for two more weeks before ending.

entry.title: Google Quantum Chip Breakthrough: Cuts Error Rate in Key Computation, Quantum Risk to Early Bitcoin Wallets in Focus
entry.summary:
Google said its Willow quantum chip used a method called "Cultivation" to reduce errors in preparing magic states — a key resource for running quantum computations — by roughly 40 times, with the research published in Science this week. The experiment reached about 99.99% state fidelity, though only around 8% of attempts passed screening.
Google said the result could lower the hardware overhead of future large-scale quantum computers, and the advance has renewed attention on the long-term quantum risk to early Bitcoin wallets whose public keys are already exposed.
Researchers said the experiment still needs to be scaled up and that real-time operation and error correction remain to be solved. Google's earlier attack-cost estimates already assumed an efficient magic-state preparation scheme, so the 40x error reduction should not be read as a 40x cut in the cost of breaking Bitcoin.

entry.title: KOSPI erases an entire year’s worth of South Korean GDP
entry.summary:
South Korea's KOSPI index closed at 5,554 on Thursday, down 7.6% for the day after falling as much as 9.3% intraday, which triggered a 20-minute trading halt — its tenth circuit breaker of the year. The decline extended losses to seven consecutive sessions and left the index more than 40% below its June peak, wiping out over $2 trillion in market capitalization.
The more than $2 trillion decline exceeds South Korea's roughly $1.9 trillion annual economic output for 2025 and the approximately $1.6 trillion value of all bitcoin in existence. The rout has also downranked South Korea's market from sixth to 10th among the world's countries, from above $5 trillion in June.
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix together account for roughly half of KOSPI's market capitalization and have driven 70% of the drawdown since the June peak. Retail investors amplified the moves through leveraged single-stock ETFs, and the finance minister apologized for introducing those products; the Financial Services Commission chairman called an emergency meeting on Thursday, instructing financial firms to "maintain vigilance" and "actively respond to ensure financial market stability and investor protection."

entry.title: Charles Schwab Fully Opens Crypto Trading, CEO Says Crypto and Prediction Markets Will Expand Transaction Revenue
entry.summary:
Charles Schwab said on October 16 that it has completed the broad rollout of Schwab Crypto to eligible retail clients, who can now trade bitcoin and ether directly through Schwab.com, Schwab Mobile and thinkorswim. The company also began phased crypto deposit and withdrawal support and plans to add Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink by the end of 2026.
CEO Rick Wurster said at the company's fall business update that crypto trading will be an important channel for expanding transaction-based revenue, alongside new businesses such as prediction markets. The article states that with spot BTC and ETH trading live and SOL, AVAX and LINK to follow, competition between large traditional brokerages and crypto-native trading platforms will intensify further.
Trades are executed and sub-custodied by Paxos at a 0.75% fee, with individual transactions ranging from $1 to $2 million, and holdings appear alongside stocks, bonds and ETFs in existing Schwab accounts. Withdrawals require new addresses to be registered with a 24-hour waiting period and are capped at three per 24 hours and $5,000 each, monthly deposits can reach up to $50 million, and the service is not available to clients in New York, Louisiana, US territories or international clients; Schwab says its clients already hold about 20% of the industry's spot crypto ETF assets.

entry.title: Karpelès Reports Ledger Implants in Devices From Two More Resellers
entry.summary:
Karpelès reported discovering malicious implants in Ledger hardware wallet devices supplied by two additional resellers, extending reported supply-chain tampering beyond the reseller previously implicated.
If tampering extends beyond a single distribution channel, users who bought Ledger devices through third-party resellers rather than directly from the manufacturer face exposure, since an implant can capture recovery phrases during wallet setup.
Earlier reports tied the implants to devices distributed by CryptoBilis, a Southeast Asian reseller, with on-chain analysis estimating roughly $93 million drained from 311 wallets after seed phrases were captured during setup. Karpelès had previously flagged implant warnings months before the wider security crisis drew attention.

entry.title: MSCI’s new rules could squeeze Strategy’s Bitcoin buying machine
entry.summary:
CryptoSlate reports that MSCI’s revised index classification rules could reclassify Strategy (MSTR) — the largest corporate Bitcoin holder — as a fund or investment vehicle, which the report says could trigger an estimated $2.8 billion of forced selling by index funds tracking MSCI benchmarks. The impact is a prospective, rule-driven risk rather than a realized event.
Strategy funds much of its Bitcoin accumulation through equity issuance, so index-driven selling pressure on MSTR would hit the mechanism the company relies on to keep buying BTC. TD Cowen analysts cited in coverage argue that an MSCI exclusion would cause short-term disruption while longer-term adoption trends remain intact.
The roughly $2.8 billion figure is an estimate of forced index-fund selling and would only materialize if MSCI reclassifies the company. Strategy’s shares are included in benchmarks such as the Nasdaq 100 and MSCI indexes, which coverage notes have funneled crypto exposure into mainstream portfolios.

entry.title: Cobo Wallet announces service shutdown on December 1; users must transfer out assets in advance
entry.summary:
Cobo Wallet published an announcement on October 16 stating that its App service will officially shut down on December 1, 2026. Users must complete the transfer of all assets and update Cobo Wallet receiving addresses they previously set on other platforms before 23:59 on November 30.
Users who still store or receive assets through the Cobo Wallet App face a hard deadline, and the announcement says balances not moved before the shutdown will be treated as the user's acceptance of a monthly account management fee.
The management fee is calculated in coin terms at 2% of the remaining account assets per month, with a monthly minimum of the equivalent of US$100. The announcement did not explain the reason for the shutdown or disclose whether other Cobo products or its institutional business are affected.

entry.title: CME lists Uniswap futures on October 19: 10,000 UNI per standard contract
entry.summary:
CME will list Uniswap (UNI) futures on October 19, with each standard contract sized at 10,000 UNI. The listing gives regulated traders a new vehicle for exposure to the DeFi governance token.
A listing on CME, a major regulated derivatives venue, opens regulated futures exposure to UNI, a leading DeFi governance token, extending institutional access to the asset class.
The contract covers 10,000 UNI per standard contract and is scheduled to launch on October 19. The source describes it as a new vehicle for regulated exposure to the DeFi token.

entry.title: Marqeta and Coinbase partner to launch stablecoin payment card service
entry.summary:
Nasdaq-listed card-issuing platform Marqeta (MQ) and Coinbase have partnered to let crypto-native and non-crypto enterprises issue bank cards funded by stablecoin balances. Coinbase handles custody of the stablecoin balances and conversion between digital assets and fiat, Base provides on-chain settlement infrastructure, and Marqeta handles card issuance, payment processing and bank and card-network relationships.
Under the described division of labour, cardholders can spend stablecoin balances at merchants that accept bank cards worldwide, extending stablecoin use beyond crypto venues onto mainstream card rails. Enterprises can also issue cards and fund card programs around the clock.
Coinbase's role covers stablecoin balance custody and fiat conversion, while Base is named as the on-chain settlement layer. Marqeta had previously issued crypto asset payment cards for Coinbase.

entry.title: Reuters: Deutsche Bank to launch crypto custody in Germany within weeks, expand to Asia next year
entry.summary:
Deutsche Bank plans to launch a digital asset custody service in Germany within weeks, initially supporting BTC and ETH, with stablecoin on/off-ramp services to follow, its corporate bank co-head Gerald Podobnik told Reuters. The bank intends to extend the custody platform to Asian financial centres next year, and separately plans to offer tokenized deposits and help clients issue blockchain-based securities such as digital bonds.
A custody offering from Germany's largest bank would add a regulated venue in Europe for institutional BTC and ETH holdings, and the stated roadmap extends beyond custody into tokenized deposits and blockchain-based bond issuance. The launch is still tied to regulatory approval, which the bank has said it expects under MiCA.
The rollout is phased: custody of BTC, ETH and selected stablecoins including USDC, EURC and EURAU first, then fiat-to-stablecoin conversion. Podobnik said the move supports the bank's target of 8% compound annual growth in corporate banking by 2028; one report placed the Asia expansion in 2027 rather than "next year", and the bank's planned Asian target markets were not specified.

entry.title: Google demonstrates quantum computing breakthrough as observers weigh Q-day implications
entry.summary:
Google demonstrated a quantum computing breakthrough, prompting observers to assess what it means for Q-day — the point at which quantum machines could break the asymmetric encryption that secures blockchain networks and other systems. Coverage frames the advance as a capability milestone evaluated against future cryptographic implications rather than the arrival of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer.
Observers weighing Q-day implications point to the public-key cryptography that secures most blockchains and digital systems in production today, which is why quantum progress by a leading lab draws scrutiny from the crypto industry even absent an immediate threat.
The development is described as a quantum computing advance demonstrated by Google, with implications assessed by observers rather than confirmed as a threat to deployed networks; it is not reported as a cryptographically relevant quantum computer capable of breaking RSA or elliptic-curve cryptography.
